ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Someone used a simple pendulum to measure the height of a mountain peak on a certain planet. At the mountain peak, a standard timing device recorded the time for the pendulum to oscillate 500 times. Then, the pendulum was moved to a location at sea level (altitude 0), and within the same time period, the pendulum oscillated 501 times. It is known that the radius of the planet is $R = 3000$ kilometers.

1. Find the altitude of the mountain.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Someone used a simple pendulum to measure the height of a mountain peak on a certain planet. At the mountain peak, a standard timing device recorded the time for the pendulum to oscillate 500 times. Then, the pendulum was moved to a location at sea level (altitude 0), and within the same time period, the pendulum oscillated 501 times. It is known that the radius of the planet is $R = 3000$ kilometers. 1. Find the altitude of the mountain.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Let the common elapsed time measured by the standard timing device be t. At the mountain peak, the pendulum makes 500 oscillations, so t = 500 T_peak. At sea level, in the same time t it makes 501 oscillations, so t = 501 T_sea. Therefore 500 T_peak = 501 T_sea, giving T_peak/T_sea = 501/500. For the same simple pendulum, T = 2π√(l/g), so T_peak/T_sea = √(g_sea/g_peak). The planet's gravitational acceleration varies as g(r)=GM/r^2. At sea level r=R, and at the peak r=R+h, so g_sea/g_peak = (GM/R^2)/(GM/(R+h)^2) = ((R+h)/R)^2. Thus √(g_sea/g_peak) = (R+h)/R. Hence (R+h)/R = 501/500, so h/R = 1/500. With R = 3000 km, h = 3000/500 km = 6 km = 6000 m.
